description: Partition splits a list into the items a predicate keeps and the items it drops, each in list order
A standing partition follows pushed items and a changed threshold that its predicate reads
code:
scores = [72, 45, 90]
limit = 60
split = scores.partition(score -> score >= limit)
scores.push(58)
limit = 50
split

description: Partition of a class population keeps population order and moves an instance when its property changes
code:
class Order(item, shipped):
    this.item = item
    this.shipped = shipped
pen = Order("pen", false)
Order("ink", true)
book = Order.partition(order -> order.shipped)
pen.shipped = true
book.map(side -> side.map(order -> order.item))

description: Partition of an empty list or an empty class gives two empty lists
Partition decides by truthiness as filter does: empty strings, zero and false go to the second list, an empty list to the first
Each side of a partition maps and counts like any other list
code:
class Shape(name, area):
    this.name = name
    this.area = area
Shape("square", 16)
Shape("dot", 1)
Shape("bar", 12)
parts = Shape.partition(shape -> shape.area >= 10)
[parts.map(side -> side.length), parts[0].map(shape -> shape.name)]

description: A class-level rule partitions the list of every instance on its own
code:
class Room(name, tiles):
    this.name = name
    this.tiles = tiles
$Room.split = $Room.tiles.partition(tile -> tile > 0)
hall = Room("hall", [3, 0, 5])
den = Room("den", [0])
hall.tiles.push(2)
[hall.split, den.split]

description: Positional destructuring names the two lists of a partition as two standing declarations
code:
xs = [3, 8, 1, 9]
kept, dropped = xs.partition(x -> x > 4)
xs.push(5, 2)
[kept, dropped]

description: Partition without a function as its first argument raises partition expects a function, even on an empty list
code:
message = ""
try:
    [].partition(5)
catch error:
    message = error
message
